title: OpenTrade: An open source harness for Claude + Robinhood
author: pinchofsoma
selftext:
We built a completely open-source trading harness for Claude Code agents that use the Robinhood MCP. 

[https://github.com/OpenTradeOSS/OpenTrade](https://github.com/OpenTradeOSS/OpenTrade)

The harness lets Claude schedule itself to react to market events or timers so you can ask it things like “Monitor the dominos next to the pentagon and accordingly trade defense stocks” - Claude will setup the script and wake itself up as needed.

Feel free to open up issues and PRs on GitHub.

comments.author: InternationalGene445
comments.body:
Went through this properly — cloned the repo and read the code, not just the README. It's the best-engineered harness I've seen come out of the Claude-trading wave so far.

What stands out: the durable scheduling layer is the real contribution — backend-owned crons plus Monitors (watch scripts whose stdout wakes the agent) that keep firing with the GUI closed. Condition-triggered wakes are something most setups don't have at all. The approval gate is done right: PreToolUse hook, the human's decision *is* the permission response, and it fails closed on every path I checked (app unreachable → deny, unattended timeout → auto-deny). Most people enforce this with prompt instructions; you built a mechanism. Also, stamping wakes as "not a message from the user" is a small detail that prevents a whole class of role-confusion failures — learned that one the hard way myself.

One constructive critique: the gate's hook config lives in `.claude/settings.json` inside the agent's own folder, and its integrity is defended by prompt ("never disable the gate"). That's prompt-level protection of the exact thing the design exists to enforce mechanically. Worth moving enforcement outside anything the agent can write to.

And the missing half, if you want a roadmap: it's all execution and safety plumbing, no measurement — no track record, no way to tell whether a strategy has edge. The harness deserves an epistemology layer on top.

Good work. Starred.
